Not sure if this guy is running Flight Simulator from Microsoft or an early version of X-Plane. Microsoft did have a Flight Simulator version that could network between PC's. I count 10 screens dedicated to the game and 1 screen to the OS. He's basically running the game on one PC and then pushing the graphics to the other PC's. His system was required in that day because GPU's were not very capable of rendering to multiple screens. In that day, the cathode ray tube was also a significantly limiting factor in the size of the image. The image is from the time when LCD screens were emerging. The lower three screens appear to be LCD screens. The top screen is running the Windows OS

I noticed that the top screen has the word "WideView" on it. It turns out that WideView is a multi-screen distribution system where a single image can be spread across multiple monitors.
